test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 8 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: ______ as a result of the 44th Constitutional Amendment to the Constitution of India.

options.text: Right to Property ceased to be a Fundamental Right
Salaries of Judges of the High Courts and Supreme Court of India were revised
Sikkim became the 22nd state of the India Union
The Preamble to the Constitution of India was amended to include the words 'socialist' and 'secular'

solution:
The correct answer is **Right to Property ceased to be a Fundamental Right**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **right to property **was no longer fundamental freedom as a result of the **Constitution (Forty-Fourth Amendment) Act of 1978,** but it remained one **under Article 300 A of the Constitution **and a human right in a welfare state.
 
• Only legal authorities have the power to take away someone's property, according to** Article 300 A.**
 
• The State cannot seize a citizen's property unless it follows the right legal procedures.
 
• Even if it isn't stated explicitly in **Article 300 A**, the responsibility to pay compensation is implied by that Article.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information**

 
• Until a change was made to the Indian Constitution in **1978**, the right to property was considered a fundamental right.
 
• Article 31 and **Article 19(1)(f) **of Part III of the Constitution's Fundamental Rights were totally abolished as part of this amendment, **the 44th to the Constitution**.
 
• This amendment was made because the government was unable to move forward with reforms and projects involving public infrastructure because citizens began petitioning the courts to stop the **purchase of private land.**
